title: When a pair-skip decoder loses a known key
question: Can a decoder built for paired skipped draws recover text encrypted with the source's one-draw skip rule, even when it has the correct key?
reader_question: Could the wrong skip rule make a correct key look wrong?
summary: In 336 source-defined planted decodes, the matched decoder recovers all runes at the stated baseline while the pair-skip decoder loses most of them despite receiving the same correct key. This is a decoder-power control, not a test of LP2's cipher.
finding: At suppression 0.83, median exact rune recovery is 100% with the matching decoder at both 240 and 400 runes, versus 37.9% and 41.2% with the pair-skip decoder. All 336 non-timing replay rows and 48 cell summaries match the pinned source output.
limitations: Synthetic known-key ciphertext from one English-derived source; no LP2 ciphertext or unknown-key search. A failure under one alignment rule cannot exclude other rules. Source score bar -5.5 is not a calibrated family-wide error rate.
next_steps: Use each proposed skip rule's own planted recovery gate before interpreting a manuscript key search.
